I need to examine the bugs more carefully.

A former member invited again hits a unique constraint error on the org-user pair. The system tries to insert a new membership instead of restoring the archived one. The invitation lookup also skips archived members, so it never finds the existing record.

Accepted members remain stuck in "invited" status because insertMember sets that state when invitedBy is present. The resolveActor check requires "active", so these users are blocked from all actions despite appearing on the members page. The seat count also excludes invited members, allowing invitations to be accepted past capacity.

acceptInvitation never checks seat quota. countPendingInvitations counts revoked and expired invites as active, which would block new accepts rather than allow them. The seat leak must come from another source.

Accepted members drop from the pending seat pool but never become active, so the seat count stays artificially low and the plan allows further overbooking. Invite links also expire after 14 hours because the expiry unit is set to hours instead of days.

The seat count includes revoked invitations because it only checks for a null acceptedAt timestamp. Expired invites are also counted since listPendingInvitations never filters them out. This leaves no available seats even when the workspace is only partially full.

Only pending invitations should hold a seat. Revoking or expiring one must immediately free that seat.

Sending multiple invites to the same email or to existing members currently creates duplicate invitations, each consuming a seat. The batch logic needs to reject case-insensitive duplicates, current members, and pending invitations for the same address. A refused batch should create no invitation at all.

Forwarded invite links are not blocked. The accepting user's email is never checked against the invitation email, so anyone can claim another person's invite and join with the invited role.

Resent invitations always default to the lowest role because resendInvitation hardcodes "member". It should preserve the original role instead.

Resend must look up invitations by ID rather than only pending ones, so expired invites can be reissued. The current revoke-then-invite flow is safe because the old link is removed before a new one is created.

Resend will look up invitations by ID without filtering for pending status. Expired or still-pending invites can be reissued, but already-accepted ones cannot.

I need to see how sessions get their active org and member.

activeOrgId should be cleared only for sessions tied to the removed user or deleted organization. Other users and workspaces must remain untouched.
Need to calculate usage seats and determine how the dashboard resolves the default organization.
Need to check usage recompute and dashboard redirect to active org.

The existing expired test uses expiresInDays: -1.

The "emits member.joined" test expects findMember to return a row, which it does for invited members. The bug is that resolveActor requires status === "active", but the spec says invited members should become active immediately upon acceptance. insertMember sets status to invited when invitedBy exists, so the accept path must update the status to active.

The comment in insertMember incorrectly claims that accepting an invitation promotes the member to active. The spec requires immediate activation instead. Options include passing null as invitedBy, adding a dedicated activate function, or changing insertMember to always set active status.

A global change to insertMember would break createOrganization, which passes invitedBy null to keep the owner active. The better approach is a dedicated `restoreOrInsertMember` function that sets status active, role, invitedBy, joinedAt, and clears archivedAt during invitation acceptance. For former members, the lookup must include archived records.

Rejoining should update the existing member record with the new invitation role, acceptance timestamp, sender as invitedBy, active status, and cleared archivedAt. The seat counter logic needs adjustment because rejoin emits member.joined, which increments usage, but recomputeUsage currently counts only active non-archived members and excludes pending invitations. The spec requires seats in use to include both current members and pending invitations.

The usage cache may be separate from the invitation seat check, which counts active members plus pending invitations. Report 2's discrepancy occurs because invited members appear in the people list but are excluded from seat counts. Making accepted members active fixes this: they will then be counted in both the member list and the seat total.

acceptInvitation never checks the seat limit before inserting a membership row. If the organization is full, resolveActor rejects the request because the member status remains invited. The invitation is already accepted and the seat is lost. This explains why members appear in the list but every page reports them as not a member.

The missing transaction means the membership row persists even if the action throws after acceptance. Invited members are not counted toward seat limits, so the quota keeps showing free seats and new invitations keep being accepted.

Setting status to active correctly increments seats via the member.joined event. The invite-side seat check counts active members, so once a pending invitation is accepted and marked as accepted, it no longer occupies a seat. The net seat count stays unchanged. The action comment claims the organization re-checks its quota at acceptance time, but if pending invitations properly reserved seats, this extra check is unnecessary.

If the organization is already full, making accepted members active would cause assertSeatAvailable to throw after they are already members. The spec does not require a rollback, so the action will remain unchanged.

Re-inviting a former member crashes because of a unique constraint. A restore function is needed.

If a valid invitation is accepted for someone who is already a current member, the system returns the existing membership without marking the invitation as used. This violates the spec that an accepted invitation must be consumed and cannot be reused. The invitation should instead be refused.

If an invitation is accepted for an already-active member with the same email, the existing membership should be returned and the invitation token consumed. If the emails differ, the action must throw because acceptInvitation only receives a userId, so the user must be looked up to compare emails case-insensitively. There is also a question about whether findOrgById returns archived organizations.

findOrgById must check archivedAt and refuse requests for archived organizations.

The invitation expiry unit should change from hours to days. The schema comment already notes this is an intentional bug. A test using expiresInDays: -1 still expires after 14 hours, which explains the "next morning" behavior.

Pending invitations are defined as not accepted, not revoked, and not expired. The count and list queries filter out revoked and expired records. Resend currently uses listPending.

Resend must look up invitations by ID without filtering out expired or revoked records. The spec requires re-sending expired invitations, so the lookup should return any invitation regardless of status. Revoked invitations are already withdrawn, so they do not need to be handled.

Resend will revoke the old invitation before issuing a new one, so duplicate checks see no conflict. The previous role is preserved during reissue. Email comparisons are case-insensitive because findUserByEmail lowercases addresses.

Batch invitations must be validated before creation. Duplicate emails within the batch should be refused case-insensitively, and any email that is already a current member or pending invite should also block the entire batch. Rate limit checks currently run before seat quota checks, which consumes rate limit tokens even when later validations fail; validating emails first prevents this.

The repository will add a `findInvitationById` lookup and a `listPending` query that excludes revoked, accepted, and expired invitations. The service will normalize emails before validating batch duplicates and checking existing members or pending invites.

The member repository needs `findMemberIncludingArchived` and `reactivateMember` methods. The accept action will check the organization is not deleted, verify the user email matches, restore an archived membership if one exists, otherwise insert a new active record, mark the invitation accepted, and emit a joined event. The resend action will revoke expired or pending invitations before reissuing them with the same role.

Notifications and digests should only target active members. When a member is removed or an organization is deleted, the session repository must clear that user's activeOrgId for sessions tied to the organization. This prevents stale defaults from persisting after removal or deletion.

Clearing activeOrgId to null is insufficient. The app must redirect sessions to another workspace the user still belongs to, not leave the column empty.
Checking whether the login flow sets the active organization.
Checking the login service for active organization assignment.
Checking the register action for a bug where activeOrgId is set after a session is created with null.
The session's activeOrgId starts null and is never set. The switch action does not call setActiveOrg.

content.thinking:
The session's activeOrgId represents the default workspace.

If activeOrgId is not cleared on removal, with-action and requireActorFor will keep using the deleted organization and fail. The clear logic should retarget sessions to another live organization when one exists. Only sessions whose activeOrgId was the removed organization are affected; other sessions defaulting to different organizations remain untouched. When an organization is deleted, all sessions for any user that default to it must be retargeted.

The `releaseActiveOrg` function will query the sessions table to find active sessions for the removed organization, then retarget each to another live organization or null. Stale `activeOrgId` values from membership removals will be corrected during cleanup. Sessions with no `activeOrgId` are unaffected.

The bug likely persists because clients redirect to `/${slug}` when `activeOrgId` still points to the deleted workspace. I will also retarget sessions during resolution if the stored organization is no longer a live membership or has been deleted.

Healing the default workspace at read time is more robust than pre-emptive cleanup. Every request will automatically retarget sessions whose active organization is invalid or deleted. This satisfies the requirement that none of their sessions keeps defaulting to the removed workspace. Sessions pointing to a valid other organization remain untouched.

I will implement both write-time cleanup and read-time healing. During resolution, if the active organization is missing or archived, I will retarget the session to another live workspace or null. A new `retargetActiveOrg` helper will update the session by token hash.
Checking the org switcher and login form to understand how organization selection is handled.

I'll examine `listOrgsForUser` more carefully.

The "keeps opening" bug likely stems from `activeOrgId` on sessions used by `withAction`. I also verified that `listOrgsForUser` filters archived members correctly.

The root cause may be stale `activeOrgId` values on sessions. The home route could redirect to an organization the user no longer belongs to. I should clear or retarget sessions when memberships are removed or organizations are deleted. Session resolution should fall back to another valid membership if the active org is gone. Login must also ensure the active org is a live membership, since a null or unpersisted value causes `with-action` to fail.

I decided not to change login unless necessary, since that behavior may be pre-existing and tests could depend on it. I also checked the orgs page redirect logic: if only one organization remains, it redirects there. I verified that `shouldFilterArchived` correctly excludes archived members because `includeArchived` is undefined.

The spec defines seats in use as members plus pending invitations.

The usage cache only counts active members, which explains the seat discrepancy. Adding pending invitations to recomputeUsage will align the count with the spec.

The UI reports usage.seatsUsed.

Pending invitations must be included in the seat count. The member.joined event increments seats, but pending invites are not yet counted there. This risks double-counting when an invite is accepted. There is no revoke event to decrement the count.

The action checks active members only, then the invitation service separately adds pending invites. If pending already fill the seat limit, the service throws. The second report is caused by invited members being excluded from the count; fixing active status resolves it. Pending invitations are not listed on the members page.

I will leave the usage formula unchanged unless tests require pending invitations in seatsUsed. The invite action already counts pending against seats, and the recompute cache intentionally excludes them to avoid double-counting with member.joined increments. This gap is pre-existing and acceptable. I will focus on the described bugs. When a member accepts an invitation, insertMember should set their status to active.

A new `insertActiveMember` helper will set status active even when an invitedBy field is present. Rejoining should call `reactivateMember`. The `findAnyMember` query must include archived records. Email matching should use `userRepo.findUserById`. If an organization is deleted, the code should throw because `archivedAt` is not null. If a user tries to accept an invitation while already an active member, the code should throw and leave the invitation pending.

If a user accepts an invitation while already an active member, the code will mark the invitation accepted and return the existing member record. It will not create a duplicate row or emit a join event, preventing a double seat increment.

Resending an invitation should preserve the previous role. The service does not validate against Zod, so a stored owner role could be passed through.

Resending an invitation will allow revoked or expired ones that have not been accepted. Revoked invitations are skipped to avoid duplicate revokes. The resend flow re-invites the same email and role. Seat counting is safe because the old invitation is revoked first, freeing its seat before the new one is issued.

Duplicate invite emails will be caught by normalizing input to lowercase and trimming, then checking against pending invitations. Active member emails will also be checked to prevent duplicates across both pools.

A `findLiveMemberByEmail` helper will join the users table on lowercase email. A `listLiveMemberEmails` helper will fetch all active member emails in a single batch query. Stored invitation emails may not be lowercased, so comparisons must use toLowerCase. The expiry predicate should check `expiresAt > nowIso` because acceptance uses `<=`. The resend flow currently relies on `listPending`, but that will no longer be used after the change.

A `findInvitationById` helper will look up invitations by organization and invitation ID. Resending an invitation generates a new token hash, which revokes the old one because SQLite enforces uniqueness on the token hash. Accepting an invitation with a different email address will return a message that the invitation was sent to another address, leaving it pending. If the workspace is deleted, the acceptance flow should report that the workspace is no longer available or the invitation is invalid. A contractor rejoin crash occurs when a unique constraint violation throws an uncaught error; restoring the member should fix this. A `reinstateMember` function is being drafted to handle reactivation.

The `reinstateMember` helper will restore a member by clearing `archivedAt`, updating `updatedAt`, and setting the role, status to active, `invitedBy`, and `joinedAt`. Changing `insertMember` to default new invited members to active would break existing tests that insert null for fillers.
